title: Olefin Metathesis Reactions of Hydrophobic Substrates in Aqueous Emulsion
author: Tyszka-Gumkowska, Kajetanowicz, et al.

steps.title: Prepare FixCatBARF catalyst
steps.instruction: Perform the ion‑exchange synthesis of FixCatBARF in a Schlenk line using an oven‑dried 100 mL two‑neck flask under argon.

substeps.instruction: Evacuate the flask for ≥15 min, then backfill with argon (≈4 L min⁻¹, 0.2 bar).
Add NaBARF (250 mg, 0.282 mmol) under argon, evacuate and backfill three additional times.
Add anhydrous DCM (70 mL) under argon (NaBARF will not fully dissolve).
Stir 15 min, then add FixCat (250 mg, 0.282 mmol, 1 equiv) in one portion under argon and stir 1 h at 20–25 °C.
Concentrate the mixture on a rotary evaporator (35 °C, 400 mbar, ≈20 min).
Spread the residue on a neutral Al₂O₃ pad (≈15 cm × 3 cm), wash with DCM and collect the green band.
Evaporate the collected solution and dry under high vacuum (≈3·10⁻² mbar, 20–25 °C, 16 h) to obtain FixCatBARF (413 mg, 0.241 mmol, 86 %).

steps.title: Extract 9‑chloro product
steps.instruction: Separate the organic product from the aqueous reaction mixture and transfer it to a clean flask.

substeps.instruction: Transfer the reaction mixture to a 250 mL separatory funnel and allow the aqueous (bottom) and organic (top) layers to separate.
Place the aqueous layer in a beaker.
Transfer the organic layer to an Erlenmeyer flask.

Return the aqueous layer to the funnel, add 10 mL EtOAc, shake vigorously, separate phases, and transfer the organic layer to a clean Erlenmeyer flask. Repeat this extraction two more times (total three extractions) until TLC (hexane : EtOAc = 9 : 1) shows no product remaining in the water.

steps.title: Scavenge catalyst residues
steps.instruction: Remove ruthenium catalyst from the combined organic extracts.

substeps.instruction: Discard the final aqueous phase in appropriate waste.
Add SnatchCat scavenger (474 mg) to the pooled organic solution and stir ≥30 min (the mixture can be stored 24 h at –20 °C if needed).

steps.title: Dry and filter organic solution
steps.instruction: Dry the organic phase, remove solids, and concentrate the filtrate.

substeps.instruction: Add MgSO₄ or Na₂SO₄ drying agent, stir gently, then filter into a round‑bottom flask.
Remove ~95 % of the solvent on a rotary evaporator (35 °C, 130 mbar, ≈15 min).

steps.title: Remove catalyst on silica pad
steps.instruction: Pass the crude product through a silica gel pad to retain catalyst residues.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a silica gel pad (≈20 cm × 3 cm) and place the crude residue on top; wash the original flask with a small amount of hexane.
Wash the product off the silica pad with hexane under vacuum filtration, ensuring the dark brown catalyst residue remains on the pad.

steps.title: Final solvent removal
steps.instruction: Evaporate the remaining hexane from the product solution.

substeps.instruction: Remove solvent on a rotary evaporator (35 °C, 130 mbar, ≈20 min).
Transfer the crude product to a small round‑bottom flask (do not use high vacuum because of volatility).

steps.title: Distill 9‑chloro product
steps.instruction: Purify the product by Kugel Rohr vacuum distillation.

substeps.instruction: Set the apparatus to 100 °C, 50 rpm, 50 mbar; collect the first fraction (unreacted material) in a bulb.
Replace the bulb, raise temperature to 160 °C, collect the second fraction.
Replace the bulb again, raise temperature to 200 °C, collect the pure product; leave the higher‑boiling yellow residue in the flask.
Optional: the Kugel Rohr can be substituted with standard vacuum distillation glassware.

steps.title: Finalize 9‑chloro product
steps.instruction: Wash, dry and weigh the purified compound.

substeps.instruction: Transfer the distilled product to a pre‑tared round‑bottom flask, wash briefly with a small amount of hexane, evaporate residual solvent on a rotary evaporator, and weigh the final material.

steps.title: Extract 11‑hydroxyundec‑2‑enal
steps.instruction: Separate the organic product from the aqueous reaction mixture.

substeps.instruction: Transfer the reaction mixture to a 50 mL separatory funnel and allow layers to separate.
Place the aqueous layer in a beaker.
Transfer the organic layer to an Erlenmeyer flask.

Return the aqueous layer to the funnel, add 5 mL EtOAc, shake vigorously, separate phases, and collect the organic layer. Repeat the extraction at least five times (or until TLC shows no product in the water) because the aldehyde is water‑soluble.

steps.title: Scavenge catalyst residues (aldehyde)
steps.instruction: Remove ruthenium catalyst from the aldehyde‑containing organic extracts.

substeps.instruction: Discard the final aqueous phase in appropriate waste.
Add SnatchCat scavenger (119 mg) to the pooled organic solution and stir vigorously ≥30 min (the mixture may be stored 24 h at –20 °C).

steps.title: Dry and filter aldehyde solution
steps.instruction: Dry the organic phase, filter, and concentrate.

substeps.instruction: Add MgSO₄ or Na₂SO₄ drying agent portion‑wise, mix gently, then filter into a round‑bottom flask.
Remove ~95 % of the solvent on a rotary evaporator (35 °C, 130 mbar, ≈10 min).

steps.title: Remove catalyst on silica pad (aldehyde)
steps.instruction: Pass the crude aldehyde through a silica gel pad to retain catalyst.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a silica gel pad (≈10 cm × 3 cm) and place the crude residue on top; wash the original flask with a small amount of hexane.
Wash the product off the pad with a 10–30 % EtOAc in hexane solution under vacuum filtration, keeping the greenish catalyst residue on the pad.

steps.title: Final solvent removal (aldehyde)
steps.instruction: Evaporate remaining solvent from the aldehyde product.

substeps.instruction: Remove solvent on a rotary evaporator (35 °C, 130 mbar, ≈15 min).
Place the crude product in a small round‑bottom flask.

steps.title: Distill 11‑hydroxyundec‑2‑enal
steps.instruction: Purify the aldehyde by Kugel Rohr vacuum distillation.

substeps.instruction: Set the apparatus to 200 °C, 50 rpm, 5–6 mbar; collect the first fraction (unreacted material) in a bulb.
Replace the bulb, raise temperature to 250–260 °C, collect the pure product; leave the higher‑boiling yellow residue in the flask.
Optional: the Kugel Rohr can be replaced with standard vacuum distillation glassware.

steps.title: Finalize aldehyde product
steps.instruction: Wash, dry and weigh the purified aldehyde.

substeps.instruction: Transfer the distilled product to a pre‑tared round‑bottom flask, wash briefly with a small amount of hexane, remove solvent, then dry under high vacuum (≈3·10⁻² mbar, 20–25 °C, 16 h) and weigh the final compound.
